newsitem.title: UK: Dlr vulnerable to mark, yen strength at Euro close.
newsitem.headline: Dlr vulnerable to mark, yen strength at Euro close.

text.p: The dollar fell to its lowest levels in almost two weeks against the mark and the yen amid worries about European monetary union and concern about Japanese fund repatriation ahead of the financial year-end, traders said.
The U.S. currency eyed the downside below 1.67 marks and 122 yen in European trading as short-term bearishness grabbed hold of the market after the dollar's recent strong performance.

"This is a short-term corrective move in a market that's lacking fresh factors to buy the dollar combined with more positive news out of Germany and some concern about EMU," said Paul Lambert, currency economist at UBS in London.
At 1535 GMT the dollar was at 1.6692/97 marks and 121.98/122.08 in late European trading on Friday.
Lambert said the dollar uptrend remained intact as long as the unit stayed above 1.6385 marks and 121 yen.

Concern Japanese companies might sell more dollars than usual to repatriate funds ahead of fiscal year-end next month was sparked by news overnight that Mitsubishi Heavy Industries was planning to liquidate all its dollar-denominated deposits, currently around $700 million, and convert them into yen.
"Japanese repatriation looks like the name of the game right now," said David Coleman, chief economist at CIBC Wood Gundy.
